meta.title: Four essential insights on using theory-based evaluation to track innovation progress
meta.topic: Heat pump perceptions and home decarbonisation

brief.intended_change: Increase heat pump uptake and contribute to Nesta's mission to reduce UK home carbon emissions by 30% by 2030.
brief.population: UK households considering home heating choices, and households hosting heat pump visits.
brief.time_horizon: Mission horizon of 2030; the supplied diagram specifies interim goals for 2027.
brief.intervention: Visit a Heat Pump enables households to take part in visits involving heat pump hosts. The team also seeks press coverage and works to grow the number of hosts and visits. Visit duration, frequency and participant dosage are not specified.
brief.context: Nesta uses a mission-led portfolio approach to home decarbonisation rather than treating each project as an isolated intervention. Its theory-based evaluation is intended to support ongoing learning and changes in strategy.
brief.outcome_first: Develop a theory of change for increasing heat pump uptake among UK households and contributing to lower home carbon emissions. Situate it within the UK's home decarbonisation challenge and Nesta's 2030 mission horizon.
brief.intervention_first: Develop a theory of change for Nesta's Visit a Heat Pump initiative in the United Kingdom. It involves households taking part in heat pump visits, supported by host recruitment and publicity, and aims to increase uptake and contribute to lower home carbon emissions.

context: Nesta's home decarbonisation work comprises four areas of focus: heat pump perceptions, installer capacity, financial incentives and consumer journeys.
The document describes systemic change in which multiple organisations contribute to final results; it does not claim sole attribution to Nesta.
The impact framework uses light-touch theory-based evaluation with lower standards of evidence, whereas the Greener Homes Content Catalyst is being evaluated using a more robust approach.

conclusions.summary: Reviewing Visit a Heat Pump's assumptions identified communications and media coverage as its most likely route to scaled impact, rather than the direct effect on individual participating households. The team consequently increased efforts to gain press coverage while also focusing on growing hosts and visits. The article presents this as an example of theory-based evaluation enabling timely strategic pivots, not as a measured demonstration that the diagram's outcomes or targets have been achieved.
recommendations: Increase efforts to gain press coverage for Visit a Heat Pump while continuing to grow the number of hosts and visits.
Monitor causal links and revisit assumptions while work is ongoing so teams can reallocate resources and refine strategy.
Match the intensity of theory-based evaluation to programme maturity, stakes and available capacity.

open_questions: The notes and article identify the supplied image as Figure 2, but its visible title is 'Summary Theory of Change for Heat Pumps Perceptions Area of Focus'. It contains five initiatives, including Visit a Heat Pump, rather than a standalone Visit a Heat Pump diagram.
No page numbers were supplied for this web article or its figure. figure_pages is therefore empty; verdict page fields are null.
The article also describes Figure 1 as the heat pump perceptions area-of-focus diagram. No separate Figure 1 image was supplied, so its relationship to the supplied Figure 2 cannot be verified.

Several arrows use shared branching connector lines without junction dots. Links through these shared lines have been expanded into source-target pairs and marked medium confidence; the figure does not distinguish each initiative's individual contribution to each connected outcome.
No outgoing connector from Get a Heat Pump to the intended-outcomes spine is clearly visible in the supplied image. None has been added.

Layer mapping follows the headings: core underpinning research=input; key initiatives=activity; intended outcomes=outcome_short; perceptions objectives=outcome_long; 2027 progress indicator=impact; 2027 mission goal=vision. The policymaker box is an indirect outcome placed below the final columns and is mapped to outcome_long.

The only causal judgement in the accompanying narrative is a comparative judgement about the most likely route to scale. Its supports coding applies to that likelihood judgement, not to demonstrated impact. No empirical effect estimates, named studies, achieved outcomes or formal overall verdict are reported.
The communications-versus-direct-participation judgement spans the pathway and cannot be assigned to a single drawn arrow; it is recorded as assumption a1 and key claim k9.
